decisive_items: extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma of the left foot treated 9 years earlier
Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a mass arising from the right frontal diploic space
Noncontrast head CT revealed a lytic lesion of the right frontal bone with hypodense soft‐tissue extension into the scalp
response.rationale: Prior extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma plus a destructive frontal diploic mass with scalp/intracranial extension strongly favors metastatic disease of that histology; R8C is the same tumor type but lacks the metastatic qualification, while other candidates are primary tumors or generic findings without the specific history link.

rejected.why: Chordoma is a clival/sacral midline tumor, not a frontal diploic metastasis; no prior chordoma.
Correct histology but does not capture the metastatic relationship to the prior foot chondrosarcoma.
Too generic, merely describes lytic bone tumor without a specific diagnosis.
No prior osteosarcoma or radiation history given; a primary skull osteosarcoma is less likely than metastasis from known chondrosarcoma.
Plasmacytoma would be lytic but no myeloma markers or systemic clues; history strongly favors metastatic chondrosarcoma.
Trauma is a red herring; lesion slowly grew and is a destructive calvarial mass.
Giant cell tumor is lytic but typically younger patients and does not explain prior chondrosarcoma history.
Initially thought lipoma but imaging and bony involvement refute simple lipoma.
No radiation history to support radiation-induced sarcoma.
Frontal chondrosarcoma is possible but less likely than metastatic spread of the known extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
